source_text:
Θεοῦ
τῆς ἐπί γε, φημὶ, τῷ Ἐζεχίᾳ γενομένης. Καὶ καθ' ἕτερον δὲ τρόπον τε- θαυμακέναι
φαμὲν τὸν Μεωδὰχ τὸ παραδόξως συμ- βεβηκὸς τοῖς μετὰ Ῥαψάκου πολιορκήσασι
τὴν Ἱε-ρουσαλὴμ, οὓς ἐν μιᾷ νυκτὶ δεδαπάνηκεν ἀγγέλου καταπταίουσα χεὶρ, ὡς
εὑρεθῆναι πάντα πρωῒ τὰ σώματα νεκρά. Οὐκοῦν ἧκον μὲν οἱ πρέσβεις, ἐπ' αὐταῖς
δὴ ταύταις ταῖς πέρα λόγου θεοσημίαις κατα- θαυμάσαντος τοῦ Μεωδὰχ τὴν Ἐζεχίου
δικαιοσύνην. Ὁ δὲ καίτοι δέον τοῖς ἐκ Βαβυλῶνος ἀφιγμένοις λαμπρὰν ποιεῖσθαι
διήγησιν τὰς κατὰ καιροὺς ἐπι- κουρίας τοῦ πάντα ἰσχύοντος Θεοῦ, καὶ τῶν παρα-
δόξων τὴν μεγαλουργίαν, ἵνα καὶ ἔτι μειζόνως τὴν θείαν ὑπεροχὴν θαυμάζοντες,
καὶ τὴν ἄμαχον ἐξου- σίαν τοῦ πάντων ∆εσπότου, διὰ τῶν παρ' αὐτοῦ μυ-
σταγωγηθέντων λόγων, ὑπονοστήσειαν εἰς τὴν ἑαυ- τῶν, τὴν περὶ Θεοῦ γνῶσιν
καταπλουτήσαντες· ἦν γὰρ οὕτω δύνασθαι καὶ ἑτέρους ὠφελεῖν ἐπαγγέλλον- τας ἃ
μεμαθήκασι· τοῦτο μὲν οὐκ ἔδρα, παρεκομί- σθη δὲ μᾶλλον εἰς ἀνθρωπίνην
φιλοκομπίαν, καὶ οὐκ ἀφ' ὧν τετίμηται παρὰ Θεοῦ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ δόξαν οἰκο- νομεῖ,
ἀλλ' ἐκ πλούτου τοῦ κατὰ τὴν βασιλείαν, καὶ μέχρι τούτων ὁρίζει τῆς ἐνούσης
εὐκλείας ἑαυτῷ τὴν δύναμιν. Ἔδειξε γὰρ, φησὶν, αὐτοῖς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ Νεχοθά·
διερμηνεύεται δὲ τὸ Νεχοθὰ τῶν ἀρω- μάτων, καὶ τῆς στακτῆς, καὶ τοῦ μύρου, καὶ
τοῦ ἀργυρίου καὶ τοῦ χρυσίου, καὶ πάντας τοὺς οἴκους τῶν σκευῶν τῆς γάζης, τοῦτ'
ἔστι, τῆς περιουσίας. Γάζα γὰρ λέξις μὲν εἶναι λέγεται Περσικὴ, δηλοῖ δὲ τὸν
πλοῦτον, ἤτοι τὴν περιουσίαν. 9Καὶ ἦλθεν Ἡσαΐας ὁ προφήτης πρὸς τὸν βασι- λέα
Ἐζεχίαν, καὶ εἶπε πρὸς αὐτόν· Τί λέγουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι οὗτοι, καὶ πόθεν ἥκασι πρὸς
σέ; Καὶ εἶπεν Ἐζεχίας· Ἐκ γῆς πόῤῥωθεν ἥκασιπρός με, ἐκ Βαβυλῶνος. Καὶ εἶπεν
Ἡσαΐας· Τί εἴδοσαν ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ σου; Καὶ εἶπεν Ἐζεχίας· Πάντα τὰ ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ μου
εἴδοσαν, καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ μου, ὃ οὐκ εἴδοσαν, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὰ ἐν τοῖς
θησαυροῖς μου εἴδοσαν. Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ 70.796 Ἡσαΐας· Ἄκουσον τὸν λόγον
Κυρίου Σαβαώθ· Ἰδοὺ ἡμέραι ἔρχονται, καὶ λήψονται πάντα τὰ ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ σου, καὶ
ὅσα συνήγαγον οἱ πατέρες σου ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης, εἰς Βαβυλῶνα ἥξει, καὶ
οὐδὲν οὐ μὴ καταλείψωσιν· εἶπε δὲ ὁ Θεός· ὅτι Καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν τέκνων σου ὧν
ἐγέννησάς γε λήψονται, καὶ ποιήσουσι σπάδονας ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ τοῦ βασιλέως τῶν
Βαβυλωνίων.9 Ἀπέσταλται μὲν ὁ προφήτης παρὰ Θεοῦ, πλὴν ἐν ἀρχαῖς Ἐζεχίᾳ
συντετυχηκὼς ὡς ἀπὸ γνώμης οἰκείας ἀφιγμένος προσποιεῖται λαλεῖν. Ταύτῃ τοί
φησι· Τί λέγουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι οὗτοι; Ἐν ἤθει δὲ πολλῷ γέγονεν ὁ λόγος αὐτῷ.
Ἀφίκοντο μὲν γὰρ οἱ Βαβυλώνιοι, τάχα που τὴν αἰτίαν, ὡς ἔφην, ἀναμα- θεῖν
σπουδάζοντες τῆς ἀνόπιν ὑποστροφῆς τοῦ ἡλίου, καὶ ἐφ' ὅτῳ
pass_a_gloss: [...] of God, that, I mean, which happened in Hezekiah's case. And in another way too we say that Merodach marvelled at the thing that happened beyond expectation to those who besieged Jerusalem with Rabshakeh, whom in one night an angel's hand falling upon them consumed, so that all the bodies were found dead in the morning. So the envoys came, Merodach having marvelled at the righteousness of Hezekiah upon these very signs from God beyond word. But he, although it was needed to make for those arrived from Babylon a splendid narration of the helps at times of the God who prevails in all things, and the greatness of the wonders, so that, marvelling still more greatly at the divine pre-eminence and the unfightable authority of the Master of all, through the words in which they had been initiated by him, they might return home into their own [land], having been enriched with the knowledge about God; for it was possible thus also to benefit others, announcing what they had learned; this he did not do, but was carried aside rather into human love of boasting, and not from the things for which he had been honoured by God does he manage his own glory, but from wealth of the kingdom, and as far as these he limits the power of the renown being in him. For he showed them, it says, the house of the Nechotha; and the Nechotha is interpreted 'of the spices', and of the oil of myrrh, and of the perfume, and of the silver and of the gold, and all the houses of the vessels of the gaza, that is, of the wealth. For gaza is said to be a Persian word, and it shows the riches or the wealth. [Lemma, Isaiah 39:3-7:] And Isaiah the prophet came to king Hezekiah and said to him: What do these men say, and from where have they come to you? And Hezekiah said: From a land far off they have come to me, from Babylon. And Isaiah said: What did they see in your house? And Hezekiah said: All the things in my house they saw, and there is not in my house what they did not see, but they saw also the things in my treasuries. And Isaiah said to him: Hear the word of the Lord Sabaoth: Behold days are coming, and they will take all the things in your house, and as many things as your fathers gathered until this day will come to Babylon, and they will not leave anything; and God said that, And from your children whom you begot they will take, and will make eunuchs in the house of the king of the Babylonians. The prophet had been sent by God, but having met Hezekiah at the beginnings, he pretends to speak as having come from his own mind. For this reason he says: What do these men say? And the word came to him with much character. For the Babylonians had come, perhaps eager, as I said, to learn the cause of the backward turning of the sun, and for what [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: … of God, the one, I mean, shown in Hezekiah's case. And we say that Merodach marvelled in another way too, at what had happened, beyond all expectation, to those who besieged Jerusalem with Rabshakeh: the hand of an angel fell upon them and destroyed them in one night, so that in the morning all the bodies were found dead (Isaiah 37:36). So the envoys came, Merodach having marvelled at Hezekiah's righteousness because of these very signs from God, which pass all telling.

Hezekiah ought to have given those who had come from Babylon a splendid account of the help that God, who can do all things, had given at each time of need, and of the greatness of His wonders, so that, marvelling even more at the divine pre-eminence and at the invincible authority of the Master of all through the words in which he had instructed them, they might return to their own land enriched with the knowledge of God. For in this way they could also have helped others by proclaiming what they had learned.

This he did not do. Instead he was carried away into human boastfulness. He did not order his own glory by the things for which God had honoured him, but by the wealth of his kingdom, and he made these the limit of all the glory he possessed. For he showed them, it says, the house of Nechotha (Nechotha means “of the spices”), and of the oil of myrrh, and of the perfume, and of the silver and of the gold, and all the houses of the vessels of his gaza, that is, of his wealth (Isaiah 39:2). For gaza is said to be a Persian word, and it means riches or wealth.

“And Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and said to him: What do these men say, and from where have they come to you? And Hezekiah said: They have come to me from a land far off, from Babylon. And Isaiah said: What did they see in your house? And Hezekiah said: They saw everything in my house, and there is nothing in my house that they did not see; they even saw what is in my treasuries. And Isaiah said to him: Hear the word of the Lord of hosts: Behold, days are coming, and they will take everything in your house, and all that your fathers have gathered up to this day will go to Babylon, and they will leave nothing behind. And God said: They will also take some of your children whom you have begotten, and they will make them eunuchs in the house of the king of the Babylonians” (Isaiah 39:3-7).

The prophet had been sent by God; yet at first, when he met Hezekiah, he made as if he were speaking on his own account, as though he had come of his own accord. That is why he says, “What do these men say?” And his words are framed with great art. For the Babylonians had come, perhaps eager, as I said, to learn the cause of the sun's turning back, and for what …

choices.why: The printed Greek spells the name Μεωδάχ; the familiar form of Isaiah 39:1 is used.

choices.term: τῆς ἐπί γε, φημὶ, τῷ Ἐζεχίᾳ γενομένης
choices.english: the one, I mean, shown in Hezekiah's case
choices.why: The help of God shown to Hezekiah, not God's presence on earth.

choices.english: the hand of an angel fell upon them
choices.why: The angel's hand strikes the besiegers (Isaiah 37:36).
Hezekiah's fault: he showed his wealth instead of telling of God's works.
ἐν ἤθει here of speech shaped to suit a character, as the prophet feigns ignorance.
